instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# task-c9599e63: noisy rectangular patches

## Validated rule

The grid has a background color and multiple rectangular patches, which may use different colors. Each patch is intended to be uniform. Some cells inside a patch may be overwritten by unrelated colors; restore them to the patch's color. Scattered non-background pixels outside the intended rectangles are distractors/noise and should be reset to the background. Preserve dimensions and valid patch cells.

Infer each rectangle from the visible consistent-color regions and its rectangular bounds. Use all patch colors, not just the largest or most frequent one. Noise inside a rectangle is corrected to the rectangle color; noise outside rectangles is cleared to background. Do not indiscriminately erase small patches or original colors that make valid rectangles.

## Evidence from three demos

- Demo 1 (27x10): background 1, color-6 rectangles at rows 2–5/cols 3–7, rows 7–13/cols 1–6, rows 17–21/cols 2–5, and rows 24–26/cols 6–8 (zero-indexed). Embedded 2/3/8/9 anomalies were restored to 6. Extraneous colored pixels elsewhere were reset to 1. Preserve all four patches, including smaller ones.
- Demo 2 (13x28): background 5; color-4 rectangles included rows 2–3/cols 4–5 and rows 3–8/cols 11–14; a color-2 rectangle occupied rows 3–9/cols 25–27. Embedded 1/9 anomalies in these rectangles were restored to patch color. Isolated noise outside patches was reset to 5.
- Demo 3 (12x26): background 5; multiple rectangular patches in colors 7, 9, and 8. For example, the color-7 rectangle was rows 1–2/cols 0–2, the color-9 rectangle rows 1–2/cols 5–6 (anomalous 6 at row 1/col 5 restored to 9), and the color-8 rectangle rows 8–9/cols 17–19 (embedded 3 restored to 8). Other isolated non-background noise was reset to 5.

These demos establish multiple patch colors and sizes, with both interior corruption and external distractors. Do not assume every isolated non-background pixel is a patch seed.

## Accepted test confirmation

The accepted task-c9599e63 test was 12x30 with background 0. Restored/retained rectangular patches included:

- color 8: row 2, cols 2–6 (7 at row 2/col 6 restored to 8); rows 3–6, cols 9–12 (including 9 at row 6/col 9 restored to 8); rows 8–9, cols 7–13.

- Scattered colored pixels outside rectangles were returned to background 0, including isolated 3/9 markers and noise such as 5/6/7/2.

The accepted output preserved all 12x30 dimensions and changed only cells supported by the rectangular-patch rule.
